scope: Owner-approved profiles, handles, privacy, local R2 avatar delivery, public SSR and staff profile/report moderation; complete existing admin/component/membership/editor regression.

ownerAuthorization.scope: Approved the profile demo and authorized local integration after confirming separate public, owner-only and staff-only routes. No remote/deployment authorization.

requiredExitGroups.design: Owner-approved isolated concept; historical prototype runs remain separate.
requiredExitGroups.storage: Populated 0009→0010 preservation, private defaults, handle/tombstone constraints and atomic rollback.
requiredExitGroups.ownerPublicApi: Strict projections, claim/field/origin/rate boundaries, PNG/JPEG/WebP metadata validation and visibility-safe R2 reads.
requiredExitGroups.moderation: Scoped real staff UI/API, reasoned audited hide/restore/remove/avatar removal, reports/dedupe/eligible auto-hide and separate outcomes.
requiredExitGroups.concurrency: Profile/admin/report revisions, actor/session/suspension/restriction/policy guards, post-commit response regression and revoked sessions during R2 I/O.
requiredExitGroups.presentation: Real owner/public/staff routes; source/built desktop/phone/WebKit workflows, no-JS SSR/metadata, strict CSP, unknown routes and separate bundles.
requiredExitGroups.regression: All original 2.0A exit groups repeated, unchanged 897 parity, full types/lint/units/build/static checks and unchanged budget limits.

sourceStability.meaning: SHA-256 stability only, not proof of correctness or test execution. Executed outcomes are the stage exit codes/logs.

limitations: Local only. No Cloudflare account/credential/resource operation, deployment or publication.
Historical 2.0/admin integration/parity/2.0A acceptance retain their original scopes and recovery distinctions.
Previous Phase 1 hardware/performance exceptions are unchanged; no hardware recertification.

Publishing, public circuit attribution/fork integration, social notifications and complete cross-subject moderation remain in 2.2/2.3/2.5/2.6/2.7; support 2.7A and final Phase 2 acceptance remain open.

Avatar cleanup is bounded and opportunistic, with durable candidates; this milestone has no scheduled global orphan sweeper. JPEG/WebP server checks validate containers/frames rather than implementing a general pixel decoder.
